title: Substitutionary Death of Christ
definition: The Substitutionary Death of Christ means Jesus died in the place of sinners, bearing the judgment they deserved so they could be forgiven and reconciled to God.
summary: The Substitutionary Death of Christ means Jesus died in the place of sinners, bearing the judgment they deserved so they could be forgiven and reconciled to God.
christFocus: Jesus stands where sinners should have stood, gives Himself as their Substitute, and secures mercy without denying God's justice.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
This doctrine focuses on the saving meaning of Christ's death: He stands where sinners should have stood and bears what they deserved. The cross is not merely an example of love or courage, though it is both; it is the saving sacrifice of the Substitute.

Scripture presents sinners as guilty before God, unable to remove their own sin. Jesus willingly takes the place of His people, carrying sin, shame, curse, and judgment so they may receive pardon and peace.

Substitution shows how mercy can be given without justice being denied. The Gospel is not God ignoring sin; it is God providing His own Son as the One who bears sin and brings sinners home.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without substitution the cross loses its saving center. Sinners need more than inspiration; they need guilt removed, wrath satisfied, and peace made with God.

This doctrine keeps the Gospel clear when culture wants a cross without judgment or a Savior without sacrifice. It tells the guilty and ashamed that Christ did not merely feel sorry for them; He gave Himself for them.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to the cross as one who needed a Substitute, not merely a teacher. Worship Christ for standing in your place, and when you teach or share the Gospel, make clear that Jesus did not simply suffer with sinners—He suffered for sinners.
